1670af6d21da9e28434f.text:  The past perfect tense tells about a past action that was completed before another past action started.  In using the past perfect tense, a helping verb had is added before the past participle. The helping verb had is the past form of has and have.

5d7902fd257843c90418.text: had worked had liked had bent had smiled had copied had gone There are several situations where the past perfect tense can be used. It is appropriate to use in the following ways.

8fb85b0a9891f582fa85.text: 1. To show that an action happened before something else in the past: 

38cb68ee7608bc6953bd.text: She stayed up all night because she had suffered insomnia.  They lost many of the games because they had not practiced enough.  Ann had met Roy before you introduced him to us at the party.  You had studied Chinese Mandarin before you moved to Beijing.

c0d166e2b6a8af29d93c.text: 2. To show that an action happened before a specific time in the past: 

ddb92cf46936e8e4759e.text: She had transferred residence before 2018.  He had never played soccer until last week.  They had gotten married before last year.  I had fallen asleep before ten o’clock.

6b43d19dded03301c94c.text: 3. Conditional perfect is used for something that might have happened in the past. 

8a7be324f0168d2cc653.text: If Karen had trained harder, she would have won the marathon.  If Marlon had studied harder, he would have passed the board exam.  If they had run faster, they could have arrived on time.  She would have met him if she had come earlier.

db6ba2382c7301cabfb3.text: 4. Reported speech is when we talk about what somebody else said. 

893935229020e64d9776.text: She said that she had taken English lessons before.  Harold mentioned that he had won in spelling bee contest several years ago  The teenager said that he had spaghetti for lunch.  Aunt Mary said that she had not received any email.

9eeb56e26b65c839427b.text: Sharon wished she had returned the package.  Billy regretted that he had forgotten his wallet  We hoped that we had bought first class plane tickets.

ce4b02193e57ce69e099.text: Note: Always remember that the past perfect tense makes it clear that one thing happened before another in the past. The order of events does not matter since the tense makes it clear which event happened first.

d6e912766ac35ed887da.text:  After Anna had eaten rice and hotdogs for breakfast, she brushed her teeth.

2eb5c165100a9749597b.text:  After – Time Marker  Anna – Subject  had eaten – Verb in past perfect tense  rice and hotdogs – Object  brushed – Verb in simple past form

577efb3ce51464fd135c.text:  Before I went to the office, I had finished some business with her.

d6034992733554382b3b.text:  I – Subject  had finished – Verb in past perfect tense  before – Time Marker  went – Verb in simple past form

e6d67c8bce4c9b332019.text:  After I had bought a phone, she came to the shop.

32a9bf2ce0c22d7286ff.text:  I and she – Subject  had bought – Verb in past perfect tense  phone – Object  after – Time Marker  came – Verb in simple past form
